newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland plans international bond issue in 1997 Q2.
newsitem.headline: Poland plans international bond issue in 1997 Q2.

text.p: Poland plans to issue international bonds in the second quarter in 1997, likely to be placed on American market, a senior finance ministry official said on Thursday.
Wieslaw Szczuka, the head of the ministry's foreign department, told Reuters the draft budget allowed the government to borrow up to $500 million on international markets.
"We are more inclined to place the issue on the U.S. market ...We're considering a possibility of issuing...yankee bonds or an issue on the Japanese market as samurai bonds," he said.
Szczuka said the final decision on the placement would be taken after assessing returns offered of each of the markets.
"One can't rule out placing the issues on both markets. If we wanted to use the whole $500 million limit, it might require two transactions or one (offering), but a big one," he said.

He said the details of the issue were likely to be decided by the end of the year, but not before the 1997 budget bill is signed into law by the president. The budget is due to be submitted by the government to parliament by the end of October.
Poland has already placed two Eurobond issues in 1995 and 1996.
The 1996 sovereign debt issue was rated as BBB minus by Standard & Poor's and BB plus by IBCA. Moody's Investors Service last year rated Poland's sovereign debt as Baa3.
